aiProvenance: Generated by Claude (Anthropic AI assistant) from the cited NASA paper. Digitised spectra were read from the vector data of the PDF figures; each reproduces the paper's reported dBA within 0.1 dB.
source: Allen, C.S. (2024). ISS Acoustics: A Status Report. ICES-2024-354 (Figs. 1-3, 7; NC ratings and sources from the text).

sources.node2: Stalled inter-module ventilation (IMV) fans: peaks in the 500 Hz and 1 kHz bands "may indicate the presence of a stalled IMV fan".
sources.jem: A peak in the 63 Hz band; a stalled IMV fan from time to time.
sources.cof: IMV fans stall when clogged with dust.
sources.lab: Pump Package Assembly running faster raised levels around the 2 kHz band (aft lab); the oxygen generation rack moved forward.
sources.mlm: Noisy cooling pumps that could not be fixed before launch; quieter replacements are being designed.
sources.mrm1: A dominant source at the nadir end, thought to be the docked Soyuz.
sources.fgb: Dust-filter and circulation fans replaced with quiet-design fans; over-life fans switched off.
sources.node1: An approved exception allows up to 59 dB at 500 Hz and 54 dB at 1 kHz.

signatures.name: Stalled ventilation fan
signatures.basis: NASA traced Node 2 peaks at 500 Hz and 1 kHz to stalled IMV fans (Allen 2024).

signatures.name: Pump running faster
signatures.basis: NASA traced a rise around 2 kHz in the US Lab to faster Pump Package Assembly speeds (Allen 2024).

signatures.name: Low-frequency source
signatures.basis: NASA reports unexplained low-frequency peaks, e.g. 63 Hz in Kibo (Allen 2024).
